transcript.content: Hi, welcome in—I'm Dr. [name]. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Doctor. Well, I came in because I just can’t seem to shut my brain off anymore. 

It’s like... it always starts with just one normal concern, like a client not responding to an email. But within minutes, my mind just spirals. I get completely convinced that I’m going to lose the contract, and then I'll fall behind on my divorce payments, and... I don't know, I just start thinking I’ll never get back to a real leadership role at work. I just can't stop the thoughts once they start.
When did you first start noticing this kind of constant, spiraling worry—did it begin around the time your divorce and related stressors started, or was it something you experienced even before that?

Well, it wasn't exactly the divorce that started it. It really began... I'd say about thirteen months ago. That's when I got fired from my last job. I thought it would get better once I got back on my feet, but even after I managed to find this current contract work, the worrying just never really let up.

Besides the work and financial concerns tied to your divorce and job loss, do you also find yourself worrying excessively about other areas of your life—like your health, your family, or things that aren't directly related to those events?

Yeah, it really does kind of bleed into everything. My mind just keeps jumping around constantly. One minute I'm stressing about the contract work, and the next it's the mortgage payments. 

But then it goes beyond the immediate finances... I worry a lot about my reputation. I'll obsess over whether people in the Bethesda tech circles think I’m damaged goods now after losing that last job. It gets so intense that just a delayed email from a recruiter can feel like absolute proof that my whole career is closing down for good. It's just exhausting.
Along with all this worrying, have you noticed physical or mental symptoms like feeling restless or on edge, muscle tension, trouble sleeping, or difficulty concentrating?

Yeah, definitely the physical stuff. I just feel... wound up almost all day. It's like my shoulders are completely locked up, just constantly bracing for bad news. And I get really restless, too. I'll find myself pacing around the house, or... if I'm on a work call, I'll be bouncing my leg the whole time, even when nothing stressful is actually happening right then. I just can't seem to physically settle down.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient describes excessive, uncontrollable worry spanning multiple life domains (work/contracts, finances, reputation, career) that has persisted for approximately 13 months, well beyond the 6-month threshold required for GAD. The worry is accompanied by physical symptoms of motor tension (restlessness, pacing, leg bouncing, muscle tension in shoulders) and a subjective sense of being 'keyed up' and unable to mentally or physically settle down. Although the symptoms began in the context of job loss and divorce, the worry has generalized beyond these initial stressors to encompass unrelated concerns (reputation, career trajectory, finances), which is more consistent with GAD than an adjustment disorder. There is no evidence of discrete panic attacks, manic/hypomanic episodes, or pervasive low mood/anhedonia to suggest an alternative primary mood or anxiety disorder, making GAD the best-fitting diagnosis.
